I purchased a 3502+tecpac in early 2025, as soon as it launched.Usage: I use it in Bangalore suburbs where there is not too much traffic often. I mainly go short distances (usually round trip10-15km) and always use sports mode. I mainly use it to buy grocery and other daily chores and ride without pillion.Build and hardware: The scooter looks good with main body (below and around seat) and front piece (below the headlight and controls) feel like metal, whereas mudguard and otherpartsseem to be of fiber. I didnt have any problem with the control buttons. There is no boot light. The opened seat doesnt close slowly enough for me to conveniently unload my grocery.Notable features: 1. Good boot space for my grocery. 2. It automatically shifts to sports mode when you accelerate hard and more power is needed. 3. It also downrates power when charge is low, and can even go at very low power after main battery reaches 0%.Personal range experience: I ALWAYS ride in sports mode and try to hit 60s and above whenever i can, which gives me a significantly less range (around70-80km) and very unreliable displayed range. Surely it'll be better on Eco. Acceleration not punchy but not bad either as it's designed for city use, and i think families. Brakes seem good, never had a problem till date.Tecpac: i think Bajaj has forgotten R&D in the hurry to launch an EV with connectivity features. It's been almost a year but my tecpac (₹5000) is still not fully activated no matter what the technicians do. I think it's a manufacturing defect and nobody at my dealership knows how to fix it. The Chetak app on my phone doesnt show any features and always shows subscription 'inactive'. The app itself has a rating of 2.0 on play store at the time of writing. I just paid for the tecpac for the sports mode and didnt really need any other features (definitely not the useless hill hold that gets accidentally triggered and lasts 3sec). Combined with one untrained, unprofessional sales staff member, the tecpac experience (except sports mode) wasted hours of my time going back and forth to theservicecenter, and i still have not a single connectivity feature, no self cancelling indicators. Additonally, I was asked to (paid)serviceit once every 3-4 regardless ofkmdriven, which doesn't make sense.ProsExcellent boot spaceDecent acceleration and 2 riding modes with tecpacGood brakesSpacious seat and foot pedals for pillionMetal body under and around seatClassic appearancePleasant localservicestaffConsTecpac activation failure and terrible Chetak app ratingRange70-80kmwhen always on sports modeAsked toserviceevery 3-4 months regardless ofkm, or else warranty will become voidNot FULL metal body as advertised.Verdict: Good scooter for city use without tech features.
